A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SurgBlood dataset and BlooDet method. All supplied pages, including figures, tables, equations, and references, support comparison. Neither PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original SurgBlood dataset analyses, benchmark evaluations in Table 1, component ablations in Tables 2–4, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results and ablations and includes an additional qualitative attention-map example.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same SAM 2-based mask and point branches, optical-flow point memory, edge generator, mutual guidance, and losses. The revised architecture illustration and operator explanation clarify the existing procedure rather than establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both train and evaluate on the same 5,330 frames from 95 cholecystectomy clips, covering the same bleeding types and two detection tasks. v2 newly identifies 41 source surgical cases. HemoSet is discussed as prior work, not evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains all 13 comparator rows, including SAM 2 with an additional point head, despite the prose changing the count from 13 to 12. The qualitative comparison also retains PAINet, PitSurgRT, and the modified SAM 2.

E3.justification: The reported annotation procedure changes from two initial annotators followed by two additional reviewers to four initial annotators followed by two additional reviewers. This is a stated protocol revision, without evidence of relabeling or rerunning experiments. The 75/20 clip split, metrics, input sizes, and 20-epoch training remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 6 adds a second input/attention/prediction example to the analysis shown in v1 Figure 8. The separate two-dimensional center-bias heatmaps in v1 Figure 5 are removed, although distance distributions remain. Component, edge-generator, optical-flow, and mutual-guidance ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for model performance. The reporting practice remains single numerical estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the matched mutual-guidance chart retain their numerical results; BlooDet still reports 64.88% IoU and 83.69% PCK-10%. Qualitative result entries change: v2 adds an attention-map example and omits the Figure 1 frame K+20 example and separate center-bias heatmaps. No numerical performance improvement is reported.

T1.justification: The explanation of Equation 8 is corrected: v1 defines the circled-dot operator as convolution, whereas v2 defines it as element-wise multiplication and separately identifies the asterisk as convolution. This resolves a mathematical-definition inconsistency with the existing architecture diagram. The remaining equations are substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain SurgBlood, joint online bleeding-region and point detection, bidirectional guidance, and superior benchmark performance. The laparoscopic title wording reflects the existing scope. Calling the dataset open-source in v2 does not establish a new contribution beyond the public release already promised in both abstracts.

C2.justification: v2 adds the assertion that bleeding-type proportions reflect frequencies in actual surgery and explicitly interprets the guidance ablation as showing superiority over a single-branch design. Existing explanations of background optical flow and cross-task guidance remain. No substantive limitations discussion is added.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses that the clips originate from 41 surgical cases and adds an ethics-approval statement. Section 5.2 changes the reported hardware from two RTX 4090 GPUs to one, without explaining the revision. Other implementation settings remain stable, and both versions still promise future code/data release without an access link.

R1.justification: v2 adds the HemoSet citation and contrasts its 857 labeled live-animal robotic-surgery frames and region-only annotations with SurgBlood's joint tasks. This provides a limited addition to dataset positioning; the other cited works and overall research framing remain.

P1.justification: v2 locally revises prose across the abstract, introduction, and method, adds laparoscopic specificity to the title, and reformats author information. Contribution bullets become an inline numbered paragraph, and dataset subsections become unnumbered headings. The overall section sequence and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The paper changes throughout from two-column to single-column layout. Dataset charts are merged, center-bias heatmaps removed, Figure 1 rearranged and shortened, and the architecture diagram relabeled with guidance-arrow legends. Attention examples expand, Table 1 gains colored highlighting, and the guidance chart gains an axis label.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity through the Equation 8 correction, source-case disclosure, direct HemoSet comparison, and clearer diagram legends. The additional attention example provides limited supporting evidence. These gains are tempered by omitted spatial heatmaps and unexplained annotation and hardware revisions; the quantitative validation remains unchanged.
